title: Strict-local global germs are invertible
statement: For a local map A→B between strictly henselian local rings [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology], let g:Spec B→Spec A and let t:Spec κ(B)→Spec B be the residue-field point. Both canonical natural transformations pulledGlobalGerm(g,t) and globalGerm(t) [def-weil-pbc-derived-global-germ] are isomorphisms of functors from abelian etale sheaves to abelian groups.

proof.text: Use the existing strictlyHenselianSections_pointedSection in StrictlyHenselianSectionsStalk. Its proof shrinks a pointed etale neighbourhood to an affine chart and localizes at its marked prime; Olivier gives a section through the full geometric point. The helper requires only a field, so it applies to separably closed fields.

Represent germs by neighbourhood sections. Pull representatives back along the pointed section for surjectivity; pull an equality on a common neighbourhood back for injectivity. Compose this germ isomorphism with evaluation of global sections on the terminal etale object.

Locality sends the closed B-point to the closed A-point. Apply the global germ argument to the composite point and transport through the existing separably closed inverse-image stalk isomorphism. The chosen pulledGlobalGerm is exactly this transport, so invertibility follows by composition.
